lessons.title: The Memorial’s Symbols and Major Padmapani Acharya

activities.prompt: What do the memorial’s circles mean, and what challenge did Acharya face?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Four Chakras
activities.body: India Gate’s memorial has four circles called the four Chakras. The Amar Chakra is called the Circle of Immortality. The Veerta Chakra has six bronze murals showing brave battle actions. The Tyag Chakra represents sacrifice and has an ancient war formation. The Raksha Chakra is called the Circle of Protection. Each tree represents a soldier who protects the nation.
keyPoints: Four circles form the four Chakras.
Amar is the Circle of Immortality.
Tyag represents sacrifice and an ancient war formation.
activities.explanation: These symbols show ideas about immortality, sacrifice and protection.

activities.prompt: A child reads about the flame and the four circles and asks what story they tell together.
steps: The original Amar Jawan Jyoti was lit under India Gate in January 1972, so the flame's story starts there.
The four Chakras matter because they show immortality, brave action, sacrifice, and protection.
The trees in Raksha make protection personal because each represents a protecting soldier.
Together, the symbols show what the memorial honors: lasting memory, courage, sacrifice, and service.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Acharya and the Memorial
activities.body: Acharya was given a difficult task. He had to capture a heavily fortified position. The memorial also carries powerful symbols. The Amar Chakra is the Circle of Immortality. The Veerta Chakra shows brave battle actions. The Tyag Chakra represents sacrifice. The Raksha Chakra stands for protection.
keyPoints: Acharya had a difficult task.
The task was capturing a heavily fortified position.
The four Chakras carry different ideas.
activities.explanation: Acharya’s task involved capturing a heavily fortified position.

activities.title: Choose the Circle’s Name
activities.prompt: What is the Amar Chakra called?
options: Circle of Protection
Circle of Immortality
Circle of Sacrifice
Circle of Battle
activities.explanation: Great choice! The Amar Chakra is called the Circle of Immortality.

activities.prompt: The original Amar Jawan Jyoti was lit under India Gate in January 1972.
activities.explanation: Yes, it was lit under India Gate in January 1972.

activities.prompt: The Raksha Chakra is called the Circle of ______.
activities.hint: This Chakra stands for keeping the nation safe.
activities.explanation: Well done! Its full name is the Circle of Protection.

activities.prompt: Match each Chakra with its meaning or feature.
pairs: sacrifice and an ancient war formation
activities.explanation: Excellent matching! Each Chakra has its own meaning or feature.

activities.title: Acharya’s Task
activities.prompt: What task was Acharya given?
options: capture a heavily fortified place
light the original memorial flame
make six bronze battle murals
protect trees in Raksha Chakra
activities.explanation: Yes! Acharya was asked to capture a heavily fortified position.

activities.title: Find the Matching Symbol
activities.prompt: Which Chakra represents sacrifice and has an ancient war formation?
options: Amar Chakra
Raksha Chakra
Tyag Chakra
Veerta Chakra
activities.explanation: Exactly right! The Tyag Chakra shows sacrifice and an ancient war formation.

activities.prompt: The memorial has four circles called the four Chakras. What do their symbols suggest together?
options: Memory, courage, sacrifice, and protection belong together.
One soldier's life passed through four stages.
The circles record the memorial's building days.
The circles show four different kinds of trees.

why.One soldier's life passed through four s: This wrongly treats the circles as one life story.
why.The circles record the memorial's buildi: This mistakes symbols for records of construction work.
why.The circles show four different kinds of: This confuses the Chakras with the trees in one circle.

activities.explanation: This combines the values shown by all four Chakras.

activities.prompt: Each tree in the Raksha Chakra represents a soldier who protects the nation. Why are so many trees shown?
options: To remember the soldiers who protect the nation.
To show how the soldiers built the memorial.
To hide the names of all the soldiers.
To show where each of the soldiers lived.

why.To show how the soldiers built the memor: The trees are wrongly treated as symbols of building work.
The trees are wrongly treated as hiding soldiers' identities.
why.To show where each of the soldiers lived: The trees are wrongly treated as maps of soldiers' homes.

activities.explanation: Each tree represents a soldier who protects the nation.

activities.prompt: The Tyag Chakra represents sacrifice and has an ancient war formation. What can a visitor understand from both parts?
options: Sacrifice was closely tied to battle.
Sacrifice happened only after the battle.
The war formation was only there for decoration.
The circle was meant for peaceful meetings.

why.Sacrifice happened only after the battle: This wrongly assumes sacrifice came only after battle.
why.The war formation was only there for dec: This treats the formation as decoration without meaning.
why.The circle was meant for peaceful meetin: This mistakes a battle symbol for a peaceful meeting.

activities.explanation: A war formation connects sacrifice with organised battle.

activities.prompt: The Veerta Chakra contains six bronze murals showing brave battle actions. A child watches them quietly. What feeling is most likely?
options: Deep respect for the brave fighters.
A strong wish to leave the room.
Curiosity about how bronze was made.
The belief that brave actions look boring.

This suggests the child is bored by the murals.
This shifts attention from courage to making bronze.
why.The belief that brave actions look borin: This wrongly treats brave actions as dull sights.

activities.explanation: The murals honor brave actions, so respect for the fighters is likely.

activities.prompt: The Amar Chakra is called the Circle of Immortality. A child asks what this name suggests. What is the best answer?
options: Those honored are remembered for a long time.
Those honored will soon be forgotten completely.
Only old battle fighters are remembered here.
Those honored all lived in one circle.

why.Those honored will soon be forgotten com: This wrongly treats immortality as forgotten memory.
why.Only old battle fighters are remembered: This wrongly links the name only to old battles.
This takes "circle" literally instead of understanding the name.

activities.explanation: The name suggests a lasting memory for those honored.

activities.prompt: A report says Acharya was given the difficult task of capturing a heavily fortified position. What does "heavily fortified" suggest?
options: The position was strongly protected.
The position was easy to enter.
The position had no soldiers.
The position was already empty.

This mistakes a protected position for an easy one.
This wrongly assumes the position had no defenders.
This wrongly assumes the position was already empty.

activities.explanation: The word suggests strong protection around the position.

activities.body: Ananda wants to join the Armed Forces, which are people serving their country. He believes people should visit war memorials, places for honouring valiant soldiers. Flowers at a war memorial reminded him of Pushp ki Abhilasha. Captain Anuj Nayyar received the Maha Vir Chakra for courage in the Kargil War. Collecting stamps is called philately.
keyPoints: Ananda wants to join the Armed Forces.
He believes people should honour valiant soldiers at war memorials.
Collecting stamps is called philately.
activities.explanation: Ananda’s thoughts show his wish to serve and honour soldiers.

activities.prompt: Why does Ananda want people to visit war memorials?
steps: Ananda believes visits matter because they honour valiant soldiers.
The flowers matter because they remind him of Pushp ki Abhilasha.
Soldiers’ sacrifices matter because they let people walk freely without fear.
So he wants visits to honour the soldiers who make freedom possible.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What does Ananda now want to do?
options: Join the Armed Forces
Start collecting stamps
Build a memorial app
Teach a poem
activities.explanation: Good choice! Ananda wants to join the Armed Forces and serve his country.

activities.prompt: Ananda believes people should visit war memorials to honour valiant soldiers.
activities.explanation: Well done! This is exactly what Ananda believes.

activities.prompt: Collecting stamps is called ______.
activities.hint: This word names the activity of collecting stamps.
activities.explanation: Great work! Philately is the word for collecting stamps.

activities.prompt: What did the flowers at the war memorial remind Ananda of?
options: The Kargil War
The Maha Vir Chakra
Pushp ki Abhilasha
The memorial app
activities.explanation: Excellent! The flowers reminded Ananda of Pushp ki Abhilasha.

activities.prompt: Soldiers’ sacrifices stop people from walking freely without fear.

activities.prompt: Match each person or thing with the correct detail.

activities.prompt: Why did Captain Anuj Nayyar receive the Maha Vir Chakra?
options: For his work with the memorial app
For his interest in collecting stamps
For his wish to honour valiant soldiers
For his courage in the Kargil War
activities.explanation: Correct! He received the Maha Vir Chakra for his courage in the Kargil War.

activities.prompt: The National War Memorial app gives information only in English.
activities.explanation: Good try! The app gives information in 21 languages.

activities.prompt: Ananda hears that people can walk freely without fear. How does he likely feel about soldiers?
options: Very grateful
Very angry
Very bored
Very disappointed

why.Very angry: This mistake confuses respect for soldiers with anger at them.
why.Very bored: This mistake ignores that soldiers help others feel safe.
why.Very disappointed: This mistake treats freedom without fear as a disappointment.

activities.prompt: Ananda wants to join the Armed Forces and serve his country. Why might he want people to honour soldiers?
options: Because soldiers’ sacrifices let people walk freely without fear.
Because soldiers enjoy taking dangerous risks.
Because war memorials are the best places to relax.
Because people can collect many stamps there.

why.Because soldiers enjoy taking dangerous: This mistake suggests soldiers fight only for excitement.
why.Because war memorials are the best place: This mistake treats memorials as places for relaxation.
why.Because people can collect many stamps t: This mistake mixes stamp collecting with honouring soldiers.

activities.explanation: Soldiers’ sacrifices allow people to walk freely without fear of threats.

lessons.title: My Dear Soldiers: A Tribute to Service

activities.prompt: Why does the poet call soldiers the great sons of their land?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Tribute to Soldiers
activities.body: This poem praises soldiers who defend the country’s borders. The poet calls them the great sons of the land. Soldiers keep guarding when everyone else sleeps, through every kind of weather. Their duty covers lonely open lands, mountains, valleys, deserts, marshes, seas and air. They give the prime of their youth to the nation. The wind chimes show respect, and the poem ends with prayers and blessings for them.
keyPoints: Soldiers defend borders and guard the land.
Their duty covers many lands, seas and the air.
The poem praises their service and sacrifice.
activities.explanation: The poem honours soldiers for their constant duty and service to the nation.

activities.prompt: Why do soldiers stay awake when everyone else is sleeping?
steps: Soldiers keep guarding, so everyone else can sleep.
They stay awake in all weather, so their guard does not stop.
They cross lonely open lands, showing how far their duty reaches.
Therefore, soldiers protect the country at all times.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Main Purpose
activities.prompt: What does the poem do?
options: It praises the soldiers
It corrects the soldiers
It teaches the soldiers
It argues with the soldiers
activities.explanation: The poem praises soldiers who defend the country’s borders.

activities.title: Soldiers and Their Duty
activities.prompt: Match each place with the soldiers’ work there.
pairs: They move across them like yogis
activities.explanation: Each pair connects a place with the soldiers’ service there.

activities.title: Guarding the Air
activities.prompt: Where do soldiers secure the air?
options: In the air
On land
At sea
In deserts
activities.explanation: The soldiers carry out surveillance in the seas and secure the air.

activities.title: The Soldiers’ Sacrifice
activities.prompt: What do the soldiers give to the nation?
options: They keep their youth for themselves.
They give their youth to the nation.
They spend their youth in markets.
They use their youth to build homes.
activities.explanation: The soldiers give the prime of their youth to the nation.

activities.title: The Wind Chimes
activities.prompt: What do the wind chimes show, according to the poet?
options: Fear of the soldiers
Pity for the soldiers
Respect for the soldiers
Doubt about the soldiers
activities.explanation: The poet believes the wind chimes show respect for the soldiers.

activities.title: The Poem’s Ending
activities.prompt: How does the poem end?
options: With prayers and blessings
With orders and warnings
With questions and doubts
With markets and shops
activities.explanation: The poem ends with prayers and blessings for the soldiers.

activities.prompt: Soldiers guard the country's borders through bad weather. The town sleeps while they give the prime of youth. How does the child feel?
options: The child feels safe and grateful.
The child feels worried and lonely.
The child feels bored and impatient.
The child feels proud and jealous.

The child may focus on soldiers' lonely open lands.
Boredom may come from seeing only quiet guard duty.
Jealousy misses the sacrifice made for the nation.

activities.explanation: Their steady guard and sacrifice make the child feel safe and grateful.

activities.prompt: The poet calls soldiers the great sons of the land. What does this show?
options: quiet fear and sadness
great pity and shame
deep pride and respect
furious anger and hatred

why.quiet fear and sadness: Fear and sadness do not match the poet's praise.
why.great pity and shame: Pity and shame are not how the poet honours soldiers.
why.furious anger and hatred: Anger and hatred do not match the poem's tribute.

activities.explanation: Calling soldiers great sons shows deep pride and respect.

activities.prompt: A soldier's duty takes them from mountains to valleys and across deserts. What can we infer about the job?
options: It stays in one small town.
It only happens near homes.
It avoids all lonely open lands.
It covers many kinds of land.

One small town cannot explain their work in deserts.
Work near homes cannot explain their duty in deserts.
Open lands are part of their duty, not places avoided.

activities.explanation: Mountains, valleys, deserts, and marshes show a wide duty.

lessons.title: Rani Abbakka and Rani Gaidinliu

activities.prompt: How did two remarkable women stand up to powerful rulers?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Two Rani Leaders
activities.body: Rani Abbakka acted when the Portuguese captured Ullal. She declared Ullal an independent sovereign country. She refused to pay tribute to Portugal and joined the Zamorin of Kozhikode. She built profitable trade with Arabia. Rani Gaidinliu was born in Manipur in 1915. She joined the Heraka movement at 13 for Naga self-rule. She led an armed uprising against British rule. Her imprisonment lasted from 1932 to 1947.
keyPoints: Rani Abbakka declared Ullal an independent sovereign country.
Abbakka refused tribute and built profitable trade with Arabia.
Gaidinliu led an armed uprising against British rule in the North-East.
activities.explanation: Remember their choices about independence, trade, and resistance.

activities.prompt: A school club is taken over by another group. How can its leader protect the club's freedom?
steps: First, the leader should refuse outside control because Abbakka declared Ullal independent.
Next, the leader should seek allies because Abbakka joined the Zamorin of Kozhikode.
The leader should build trade because Abbakka traded profitably with Arabia.
Together, these choices protect freedom because Abbakka defied Portugal without paying tribute.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What did Rani Abbakka declare about Ullal?
options: An independent country
A Portuguese colony
A trading base
A British territory
activities.explanation: She declared that Ullal was an independent sovereign country.

activities.prompt: Rani Abbakka built a profitable trading relation with ______.
activities.hint: She defied the Portuguese while building this trade.
activities.explanation: She defied the Portuguese and built a profitable trading relation with Arabia.

activities.prompt: Match each person or place with the matching detail.
pairs: joined forces with the Zamorin of Kozhikode
belonged to the Rongmei or Kabui tribe
was born in Tamenglong district of Manipur
activities.explanation: Each pair links a person or place with a detail from the lesson.

activities.prompt: Why was Gaidinliu given the title Rani?
options: For her courage
For profitable trade
For helping the Portuguese
For trading with Arabia
activities.explanation: She received the title for her courage and also received the Padma Bhushan.

activities.prompt: Match each choice with its matching detail.
pairs: refusing to pay tribute to Portugal
joining forces with the Zamorin of Kozhikode
activities.explanation: These details show the important choices and honours of both leaders.

activities.prompt: Put Gaidinliu's life events in the correct order.
items: She was born in Tamenglong district of Manipur in 1915
At 13, she joined the Heraka movement
The British imprisoned her for life from 1932
Her imprisonment ended in 1947
activities.explanation: The order follows her birth, joining Heraka, imprisonment, and its end.

activities.prompt: Ullal is captured by the Portuguese. Abbakka refuses to pay tribute. How does she likely feel?
options: She feels determined to protect Ullal's freedom from Portugal.
She feels proud that Portugal now controls Ullal.
She feels relieved that she has accepted Portuguese tribute.
She feels safe because Portugal no longer threatens her.

why.She feels proud that Portugal now contro: This mistake treats Portuguese capture as something she welcomed.
why.She feels relieved that she has accepted: This mistake reverses her refusal to pay tribute.
why.She feels safe because Portugal no longe: This mistake treats her defiance as fear of Portuguese power.

activities.explanation: Refusing tribute shows that she wants to protect Ullal's freedom.

activities.prompt: Ullal faces Portuguese control. Abbakka joins forces with the Zamorin of Kozhikode. Why is this wise?
options: The alliance gives her another ruler's support against Portugal.
The alliance makes Ullal become part of Kozhikode itself.
The alliance means she no longer needs to protect Ullal.
The alliance forces Portugal to end its Arabian trade.

why.The alliance makes Ullal become part of: This mistake confuses joining forces with losing Ullal's independence.
why.The alliance means she no longer needs t: This mistake thinks an ally makes protection unnecessary.
why.The alliance forces Portugal to end its: This mistake connects the alliance to Arabia's trade without evidence.

activities.explanation: Joining the Zamorin gives Abbakka another ruler's support.

activities.prompt: Abbakka defies the Portuguese and builds a profitable trading relation with Arabia. What does this suggest?
options: She can use trade to strengthen Ullal while resisting Portugal.
She has ended all trade with lands outside Ullal.
She now accepts that Portugal should control Ullal's trade.
She must stop working with any ruler besides herself.

why.She has ended all trade with lands outsi: This mistake mistakes one new trade relation with ending all trade.
why.She now accepts that Portugal should con: This mistake reverses her resistance to Portuguese control.
why.She must stop working with any ruler bes: This mistake confuses refusing Portugal with refusing all allies.

activities.explanation: Her profitable trade gives her strength while she resists Portugal.

activities.prompt: At 13, Gaidinliu joins the Heraka movement for Naga self-rule. What does this show about her?
options: She is willing to act for freedom while still very young.
She prefers waiting until she is much older to help.
She wants the British to keep control over the North-East.
She thinks Naga self-rule needs no action from her.

why.She prefers waiting until she is much ol: This mistake treats her decision to join as a wish to wait.
why.She wants the British to keep control ov: This mistake reverses her struggle against British rule.
why.She thinks Naga self-rule needs no actio: This mistake ignores the action she took at 13.

activities.explanation: Her early action shows a strong wish to support Naga self-rule.

activities.prompt: Gaidinliu leads an uprising and is imprisoned from 1932 to 1947. What do these facts show?
options: She kept fighting for her cause despite losing her freedom.
She stopped caring about her cause once prison began.
She wanted British rule after joining the Heraka movement.
She showed courage only after her prison term ended.

why.She stopped caring about her cause once: This mistake assumes prison made her abandon her cause.
why.She wanted British rule after joining th: This mistake reverses her wish to oppose British rule.
why.She showed courage only after her prison: This mistake places her courage only after the events described.

activities.explanation: Her title for courage fits her continued fight despite prison.

activities.prompt: Abbakka calls Ullal an independent sovereign country. She refuses tribute to Portugal. What must 'sovereign' mean here?
options: Ullal has its own authority and is not ruled by Portugal.
Ullal must obey Portugal but may keep its own trade.
Ullal belongs to the Zamorin but may choose its own trade.
Ullal may reject tribute but must follow all outside rules.

why.Ullal must obey Portugal but may keep it: This mistake separates trade freedom from political freedom.
why.Ullal belongs to the Zamorin but may cho: This mistake confuses an ally with the ruler of Ullal.
why.Ullal may reject tribute but must follow: This mistake allows refusing tribute while denying real independence.

activities.explanation: Calling Ullal sovereign and refusing tribute show its own authority.

activities.context: During a school visit to the National War Memorial near India Gate, a guide shows the group the tablets and explains that each brick in the memorial is called a tablet. The tablets carry the names of soldiers who fought for India. The memorial covers more than 40 acres and was built between April 2018 and February 2019. The guide asks the students what the names and the memorial help us remember.
activities.prompt: A visitor calls a tablet “just a brick.” What is the best response?
options: It is a tablet carrying a soldier’s name, so it helps us remember someone who fought for India.
It is only building material, so the name written on it has no special importance.
It shows that every soldier named won India’s highest wartime gallantry medal.
It is mainly useful for showing the size of the memorial rather than remembering soldiers.

why.It is only building material, so the nam: The student wrongly treats the tablet as ordinary building material.
